name: Chef-plated course
summary: The chef arranges each portion on its own plate in the kitchen, and the waiter brings it to the guest without any change.
how: Warm a large plate of 280 to 320 mm and keep the rim clean.
Put the sauce on the plate first, and then the main piece, in one place that the chef chooses.
Leave 40 to 55 per cent of the plate empty, and set no more than three garnishes.
Check the plate at the pass before it leaves the kitchen.

origin.note: The chefs of the nouvelle cuisine, among them the Troisgros brothers and Paul Bocuse, put the plating in the kitchen and not at the table.

adoptions.via: Michel Guérard set small steamed portions on wide plates for the guests of the spa.
Chinois on Main and later Roy's and Nobu plated an Asian main piece in a modern shape on a wide plate.
